summary: End-to-end validation of the multi-slip discrepancy fix (NIKAVI #723 regression). Backend: GET /api/orders?status_filter=Pending for the real NIKAVI order 3ebf5a1b now surfaces ALL 4 qualifying slips (707, 723, 754, 766) with per-slip items and quantity-aware usable; slip 723 usable correctly includes 'SIDE STAND HONDA SHINE BS6': 150; discrepancy.usable_pcs=2849, pending_after=6546. POST /api/orders/discrepancy-resync?dry_run=true returns count=39 with NIKAVI row action='clear' and slip_lines for 707/723/754/766; MD5 snapshots of orders+dispatches collections are IDENTICAL before/after proving zero mutation. QA scenario created from scratch (QA TEST customer + 2 off-order dispatches on different SKUs/dates + 1 order today) → flagged with BOTH slips; usable A=40 on older slip, B=30 on newer. POST .../resolve-discrepancy {action:'clear', dispatch_ids:[old,new]} is quantity-aware: order items become ONLY {A:60} (B line fully consumed and removed, A reduced 100→60), status stays Pending, BOTH slips get the order id in order_ids. POST .../undo-discrepancy fully reverts (A:100, B:30 restored, order_ids removed from both slips, discrepancy with both slips re-appears). Scoped resync dry_run=false {order_ids:[qa]} applies ONLY to the QA order (reduces A 100→75), real NIKAVI order items byte-identical before/after. Frontend (/orders, Discrepancy filter): disc-slips-3ebf5a1b-ae4b-412c-9e94-990ef9d96cb8 renders 4 rows (disc-slip-...-707, 723, 754, 766) each with green 'Will apply: N pcs' badge and SIDE STAND HONDA SHINE BS6:150 visible on slip 723; disc-usable-total shows 'On Clear: 2849 pcs applied · Pending after 6546'; clicking a slip number opens the Dispatch Slip preview dialog (role=dialog present). Resync card: disc-resync-check-btn fires dry-run; disc-resync-row-3ebf5a1b-... header lists 'Slip #707, #723, #754, #766' and badge 'Pending 9415 → 6546'; disc-resync-cancel-btn removes the result panel. NO Apply/Clear/Update/Keep/Delete action was ever clicked on real orders.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py list_orders: 'best' slip is still chosen as the most-recent and only its 'items' feed the top-level discrepancy brief (Dispatched on <date> (Slip #<best>)). The newly-attached 'slips' array is correct, but any UI/export that reads the top-level fields (older PDF export, Hindi alert texts referencing a single slip) will keep showing only the latest slip. Recommend returning top-level slip_no/dispatched_at as the OLDEST qualifying slip (matches the 'first evidence' intuition) OR dropping the top-level fields entirely in favour of 'slips[]'.

list_orders detection loop is O(orders × customer_dispatches) with a per-order _reconcile_customer_orders call for usable_pcs. For 39 flagged orders on this dataset the GET /api/orders?status_filter=Pending request takes ~2-3s. Consider memoising _reconcile_customer_orders per customer_id (currently invoked once per unique customer that has a discrepancy – OK – but internally re-walks every dispatch). Add an index on dispatches.customer_id + dispatched_at if not present.

resolve_discrepancy clear path now accepts dispatch_ids (list) but the request model still exposes the single dispatch_id for backward compatibility. The frontend sends BOTH; backend prefers the list. Add Pydantic validator so that dispatch_id if present is a member of dispatch_ids (defence-in-depth against accidentally applying a slip that's not in the shown multi-slip list).

discrepancy_resync returns 'missed' count but the public endpoint doesn't restrict dispatch_slip side-effects – a resync run that reconciles orders also toggles order_fully_dispatched / order_ids on dispatches. Documented behaviour, but worth logging a server-side AUDIT entry per order that is modified (currently only the per-order activity feed captures the change).

rca of the issue: FIX IS CORRECT. Original bug: list_orders only populated the single most-recent qualifying slip in 'discrepancy.slip_no'. New code builds an 'all_slips' list of EVERY dispatch within disc_window that shares an SKU and is dated before the order's created_at, sorts by dispatched_at ASC, and attaches it as discrepancy.slips (with per-slip 'items' and quantity-aware 'usable' computed via _reconcile_customer_orders(allow_before={oid: {all dispatch_ids}})). 'clear' uses the same allow_before={oid:[dispatch_ids]} + only={oid} so multi-slip resolution is reconciled in one shot and quantity-aware (fully-consumed lines removed, partials reduced). undo_discrepancy snapshot/restore already covers multi-dispatch via the dispatches_before list. Resync surfaces the same multi-slip set to the UI confirmation panel before applying.
